title.value: Brain-spinal cord interaction in long-term motor sequence learning in human: An fMRI study
title.justification: The title is directly mentioned at the beginning of the research paper.
title.quote: Brain-spinal cord interaction in long-term motor sequence learning in human: An fMRI study

analysis.description: This study investigates the role of the spinal cord in long-term motor sequence learning in humans using fMRI. The authors explore how spinal-cerebral functional plasticity evolves over extended training periods and how it interacts with brain networks during the learning process.

type.justification: The study involves experiments and data collection using fMRI to study brain-spinal cord interactions during motor sequence learning.
type.quote: Here, we investigated spinal–cerebral functional plasticity associated with learning of a specific sequence of visually-guided joystick movements...

name.justification: The research involves brain and spinal cord interaction in motor sequence learning, a topic that is typically studied within cognitive neuroscience.
name.quote: A plethora of neuroimaging studies has sought to provide insights into the neurofunctional mechanisms mediating motor learning capacities in humans...

name.justification: The study uses fMRI to investigate brain and spinal cord changes during motor sequence learning.
name.quote: we used an innovative functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) protocol, during which we scanned the brain and cervical spinal cord simultaneously...

name.justification: The core focus is on understanding how humans learn motor sequences over time, specifically the neural correlates involved in this process.
name.quote: Motor sequence learning (MSL) is one such skill; it refers to the process during which simple, stereotyped movements come to be performed effortlessly...
